summary:
We developed EVA, an offline, two-tier health monitoring software ecosystem for deep-space missions where Earth communication lags up to 40 minutes and GPS does not exist. The system integrates three components: a suit-level Biometric Flight Recorder (BFR) that logs vital signs alongside radiation and suit pressure; a Crew Mobile App for daily physical and mental health check-ins; and EVA Station, a local command dashboard powered by our Surveillance Priority Index (IPV).

EVA addresses the challenge by shifting medical oversight from Earth to the spacecraft and suit. Using zero-latency local processing, it ranks crew members by acute risk and accumulated vulnerability, spotlighting the astronaut in greatest danger up to 10 minutes before a vital collapse. During extravehicular emergencies, it diagnoses root causes even in signal blackouts and uses GPS-free signal timing (Time-of-Flight) to alert nearby teammates to lethal hazard perimeters to the meter.

This is critical because it prevents cascade casualties in uncharted environments and protects billion-dollar missions as a "plug-and-play" intelligence layer for existing NASA sensors—while offering immediate commercial applications in offline terrestrial sectors like underground mining and emergency rescue.
details:
1.- What EVA Does & How It Works

EVA (by Out World Theory) is an offline, zero-latency astronaut health and survival system built for deep-space missions with up to 40-minute Earth communication delays and no GPS. It connects three layers:

Explorers (Suit & Biometric Flight Recorder): Tracks heart rate, SpO₂, core temperature, respiration, HRV, suit pressure, and radiation. Its local Biometric Flight Recorder (BFR) diagnoses root causes during signal blackouts, while GPS-free Time-of-Flight signal timing alerts nearby teammates to lethal hazard perimeters to the meter.

Crew Mobile App: Logs daily physical and mental health check-ins inside the spacecraft to establish individual readiness baselines.

EVA Station (Command Dashboard): Centralizes telemetry in an offline local database and ranks crew members using our Surveillance Priority Index (IPV) (acute risk + accumulated vulnerability), spotlighting the astronaut in greatest danger.

2.- Benefits & Intended Impact

Space Missions: Cuts emergency reaction from 40 minutes to milliseconds, allows intervention up to 10 minutes before physiological collapse, and prevents cascade crew casualties.

Commercial Earth Dual-Use: Ready to deploy in offline, high-risk industries such as underground mining, offshore oil rigs, and emergency rescue teams.

3.- Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software

Frontend & Dashboard: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (interactive EVA Station command center, mobile Crew App interface, and real-time telemetry simulator).

Backend & Data: Local web server, JSON telemetry streaming, and offline local database storage.

Design & Documentation: Canva (7-slide pitch deck) and generative AI tools (English copyediting and system architecture diagramming).

4. Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Plug-and-Play Intelligence: Upgrades existing NASA suit sensors instead of requiring costly hardware redesigns.

Operational Constraints: Accounted for total signal blackouts inside craters, cognitive load on non-medical operators, and "Space-Normal" physiological baselines.
